text: In the Gulf of Mexico, the Deepwater Horizon oil spill caused $2.5 billion in losses for the commercial fishing industry. The U.S. Travel Association estimated that the economic impact on tourism across the Gulf Coast over a three-year period could exceed $23 billion, in a region supporting over 400,000 travel industry jobs that generate $34 billion in annual revenue. On 30 April 2010, President Barack Obama ordered a halt to new offshore drilling leases and authorized an investigation of 29 oil rigs to determine the cause of the disaster. A six-month moratorium on offshore drilling below 500 ft (150 m) of water was enforced by the U.S. Department of the Interior, suspending work on 33 rigs, and a group of affected companies formed the Back to Work Coalition. On 22 June, a U.S. federal judge, Martin Leach-Cross Feldman of the Eastern District of Louisiana, ruled in Hornbeck Offshore Services LLC v. Salazar that the moratorium was too broad, arbitrary, and inadequately justified, and the ban was lifted in October 2010. Prior to the spill, on 31 March 2010, Obama ended a ban on oil and gas drilling along most of the East Coast and northern Alaska to support an energy and climate bill and reduce foreign oil and gas imports. On 28 April 2010, Canada’s National Energy Board issued a letter to oil companies asking them to explain their opposition to safety rules requiring same-season relief wells. On 3 May, California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger withdrew support for expanded offshore drilling in California. On 8 July, Florida Governor Charlie Crist called for a special session to draft a constitutional amendment banning offshore drilling in state waters, which the legislature rejected on 20 July. In October 2011, the U.S. Department of the Interior’s Minerals Management Service was dissolved due to poor oversight, replaced by three new agencies: the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement, the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management, and the Office of Natural Resources Revenue. In March 2014, BP was allowed to bid for oil and gas leases again. On 30 April, President Obama sent the Secretaries of Interior and Homeland Security, the EPA Administrator, and NOAA to the Gulf Coast to assess the disaster. In his 15 June speech, Obama stated, "This oil spill is the worst environmental disaster America has ever faced... We will fight this spill with everything we've got for as long as it takes. We will make BP pay for the damage their company has caused. And we will do whatever's necessary to help the Gulf Coast and its people recover from this tragedy." Interior Secretary Ken Salazar said, "Our job basically is to keep the boot on the neck of British Petroleum." Some observers suggested the Obama administration was overly aggressive, with some BP investors viewing it as an attempt to deflect criticism of Obama’s crisis management. Rand Paul accused Obama of being anti-business and "un-American." Public opinion polls in the U.S. were generally critical of how President Obama and the federal government handled the disaster and were extremely critical of BP’s response. Across the U.S., thousands participated in dozens of protests at BP gas stations and other locations, reducing sales at some stations by 10% to 40%. An academic study noted that the severity of disruption significantly influenced the social construction of the event, as policy actors were ill-equipped to manage the challenges at all levels. The petroleum industry claimed disasters are infrequent and that this spill was an isolated incident, rejecting claims of lost industry credibility. The American Petroleum Institute (API) stated that offshore drilling is important for job creation and economic growth. CEOs from the top five oil companies agreed to improve safety, and API announced the creation of an offshore safety institute separate from its lobbying operations. The Organization for International Investment warned that heated rhetoric could damage British companies’ reputations in the U.S. and spark U.S. protectionism affecting government contracts, political donations, and lobbying. In July 2010, President Obama issued an executive order citing the Deepwater Horizon spill, adopting recommendations from the Interagency Ocean Policy Task Force and establishing the National Ocean Council, which brought together federal committees and departments on ocean issues to work with a new conservation and resource management committee. In June 2018, President Donald Trump revoked this executive order to roll back bureaucracy and benefit "ocean industries that employ millions of Americans." In the UK, there was anger at U.S. media for using the term "British Petroleum," which was discontinued in 1998 when British Petroleum merged with Amoco to form BP Amoco. It was claimed the U.S. was "dumping" blame on the British public, with calls for British Prime Minister David Cameron to protect British interests. British pension fund managers, who hold large BP shares and rely on its dividends, accepted that while BP had to pay compensation, the cost to its market value from Obama’s criticism outweighed direct clean-up costs. Initially, BP downplayed the incident; CEO Tony Hayward called the oil and dispersant amounts "relatively tiny" compared to the "very big ocean." Later, he faced criticism when he said the spill disrupted Gulf Coast residents and added, "You know, I'd like my life back." BP’s chief operating officer Doug Suttles contradicted claims of an underwater plume, stating, "It may be down to how you define what a plume is here… The oil that has been found is in very minute quantities." In June 2010, BP launched a PR campaign and successfully bid for search terms related to the spill on Google and other search engines so that the first sponsored result linked to its website. On 26 July 2010, CEO Tony Hayward was to resign and was replaced by Bob Dudley, an American citizen who previously worked for Amoco. Hayward became a highly controversial public figure; in May 2013, he was honored as a "distinguished leader" by the University of Birmingham, but the award ceremony was repeatedly interrupted by jeers and walk-outs and protests from People & Planet members. In July 2013, Hayward received an honorary degree from Robert Gordon University, which Friends of the Earth Scotland described as a "sick joke" and "a very serious error of judgement," with the student body president expressing disappointment. The U.S. government rejected offers of cleanup help from Canada, Croatia, France, Germany, Ireland, Mexico, the Netherlands, Norway, Romania, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and the United Nations. The U.S. State Department listed 70 assistance offers from 23 countries, all initially declined, but eight were later accepted. The U.S. Coast Guard actively requested skimming boats and equipment from several countries. The U.S. Deepwater Horizon investigation included several investigations and commissions, including reports by: the Republic of the Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator, BP’s internal investigation, a U.S. Coast Guard and Minerals Management Service investigation launched on 22 April 2010, a request from the U.S. administration on 11 May for the National Academy of Engineering to conduct an independent technical investigation, and the establishment on 22 May of the National Commission on the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill and Offshore Drilling to "consider the root causes of the disaster and offer options on safety and environmental precautions." The U.S. Attorney General Eric Holder announced an investigation on 1 June 2010. The House Committee on Energy and Commerce conducted hearings, including those of Tony Hayward and heads of Anadarko and Mitsui’s exploration unit. According to the congressional investigation, the rig’s blowout preventer, built by Cameron International Corporation, had a hydraulic leak and a failed battery, and therefore failed. On 8 September 2010, BP released a 193-page report on its website placing some blame on BP, Halliburton, and Transocean. The report found that on 20 April 2010, managers misread pressure data and approved replacing drilling fluid with seawater, which was not heavy enough to prevent gas from igniting, causing the explosion. BP, Transocean, and Halliburton were each partly to blame. Responding, Transocean and Halliburton placed all blame on BP. On 9 November 2010, the Oil Spill Commission reported that there had been "a rush to completion" and criticized poor management decisions, stating, "There was not a culture of safety on that rig." The National Commission on the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill and Offshore Drilling released a final report on 5 January 2011. The panel found that BP, Halliburton, and Transocean attempted to work more cheaply, which helped trigger the explosion and subsequent leakage. The report stated that "whether purposeful or not, many of the decisions that BP, Halliburton, and Transocean made that increased the risk of the Macondo blowout clearly saved those companies significant time (and money)." BP stated that "even prior to the conclusion of the commission's investigation, BP instituted significant changes designed to further strengthen safety and risk management." Transocean blamed BP for making the decisions before the explosion and government officials for permitting them. Halliburton stated it acted only upon BP’s orders when injecting cement into the well and criticized BP for failing to run a cement bond log test. The report accused BP of nine faults, including not using a diagnostic tool to test cement strength, ignoring a failed pressure test, and not plugging the pipe with cement. The report concluded that "notwithstanding these inherent risks, the accident of April 20 was avoidable" and that "it resulted from clear mistakes made in the first instance by BP, Halliburton and Transocean, and by government officials who, relying too much on industry's assertions of the safety of their operations, failed to create and apply a program of regulatory oversight that would have properly minimized the risk of deepwater drilling." The panel also noted that government regulators lacked sufficient knowledge or authority to notice cost-cutting decisions. On 23 March 2011, BOEMRE (former MMS) and the U.S. Coast Guard published a forensic examination report on the blowout preventer by Det Norske Veritas, concluding that the primary cause of failure was that the blind shear rams failed to fully close and seal due to a portion of drill pipe buckling between the shearing blocks. A U.S. government report issued in September 2011 stated that BP is ultimately responsible for the spill, with Halliburton and Transocean sharing some blame. The report identified the main cause as a defective cement job, and stated that Halliburton, BP, and Transocean were responsible in different ways. It noted that although the events leading to the sinking of Deepwater Horizon were set in motion by the failure to prevent a well blowout, the investigation revealed numerous systems deficiencies and acts and omissions by Transocean and its crew that adversely impacted the ability to prevent or limit the disaster. A central cause of the blowout was the failure of a cement barrier allowing hydrocarbons to flow up the wellbore, through the riser, and onto the rig, resulting in the blowout. The loss of life and subsequent pollution of the Gulf of Mexico resulted from poor risk management, last-minute changes to plans, failure to observe and respond to critical indicators, inadequate well control response, and insufficient emergency bridge response training by companies and individuals responsible for drilling at the Macondo well and for the operation of the drilling platform. On 16 June 2010, after BP executives met with President Obama, BP announced and established the Gulf Coast Claims Facility (GCCF), a $20 billion fund to settle claims from the Deepwater Horizon spill, covering natural resource damages, state and local response costs, and individual compensation, but not fines or penalties. Prior to the GCCF, emergency compensation was paid by BP from an initial facility. The GCCF was administered by attorney Kenneth Feinberg and began accepting claims on 23 August 2010. On 8 March 2012, after BP and a team of plaintiffs' attorneys agreed to a class-action settlement, a court-supervised administrator, Patrick Juneau, took over administration. Over one million claims from 220,000 individual and business claimants were processed, and more than $6.2 billion was paid out, with 97% of payments going to claimants in the Gulf States. In June 2012, the GCCF settlement was replaced by a court-supervised settlement program, during which an additional $404 million in claims were paid. The GCCF and Feinberg were criticized for the amount and speed of payments and a lack of transparency. An independent audit of the GCCF, approved by the Senate on 21 October 2011, found that 7,300 claimants were wrongly denied or underpaid, resulting in about $64 million in additional payments. The Mississippi Center for Justice provided pro bono assistance to 10,000 people to help them navigate the claims process. In a New York Times opinion piece, Stephen Teague, staff attorney at the Mississippi Center for Justice, argued that BP had become "increasingly brazen" in "stonewalling payments," noting that tens of thousands of Gulf residents still had not been fully compensated, and many were struggling financially, especially low-wage workers in fishing and service industries seeking compensation for lost wages and jobs for three years. In July 2013, BP filed a motion in court to freeze payments on tens of thousands of claims, arguing that a staff attorney from the Deepwater Horizon Court-Supervised Settlement Program had improperly profited from claims filed by a New Orleans law firm. The attorney is said to have received portions of settlement claims for clients he referred to the firm. Federal Judge Barbier refused to halt the settlement program, stating he had not seen evidence of widespread fraud and that he was "offended by what he saw as attempts to smear the lawyer administering the claims." By 26 May 2010, over 130 lawsuits had been filed against one or more of BP, Transocean, Cameron International Corporation, or Halliburton Energy Services, though observers expected these to be combined into one multidistrict litigation. On 21 April 2011, BP issued $40 billion in lawsuits against rig owner Transocean, cementer Halliburton, and blowout preventer manufacturer Cameron, alleging failed safety systems and irresponsible contractor behavior, including claims that Halliburton failed to properly use modeling software to analyze safe drilling conditions. The firms denied the allegations. On 2 March 2012, BP and plaintiffs agreed to settle roughly 100,000 claims filed by individuals and businesses affected by the spill.

---

### 🔍 Step 2: Apply Article 2 – The Definition of a Contract

**Article 2 (Definition):**  
> "For the purpose of this Law, a contract means an agreement on the establishment, alteration or termination of a civil right-obligation relationship between natural persons, legal persons or other organizations as subjects with equal status. Agreements on establishing such personal relationships as marriage, adoption and guardianship shall be governed by the provisions of other laws."

#### How to use this as a filter:
- This definition acts as a **clear boundary** for what *is* a contract under this law.
- Any scenario involving **personal relationships** (marriage, adoption, guardianship) is **excluded** from the scope of the Contract Law and must be governed by other laws (e.g., Marriage Law, Adoption Law).
- Only agreements between **equal-status parties** (natural persons, legal persons, or organizations) that create **civil rights and obligations** are covered.

### 🟦 **Blue – First Two Sets (Team Participation & Format)**  
*Applies to the initial rounds: Set 1 and Set 2*

- **Match Format**:

  - No away goal rule applies.  
  - If teams are tied, the match proceeds to **extra time**, and if still tied, a **penalty shootout**.

> ✅ **Visual cue**: Blue = foundational phase with growing team pool; all matches are single-leg.

---

### 🟩 **Green – Knockout Rounds (Team Participation & Format)**  
*Applies to rounds 3 to 5 (after the first two sets)*

- **Team Participation**:  
  - Teams are progressively eliminated in a **knockout format**.  
  - Only the winners advance to the next round.  
  - No new teams join; the number of teams halves each round (e.g., 56 → 28 → 14 → 7 → 4).

- **Match Format**:  
  - All matches remain **single-leg**.  
  - Ties go to extra time, then penalty shootout (no away goals).

> ✅ **Visual cue**: Green = knockout progression; consistent single-leg format; teams are reduced by half.

---

### 🟥 **Red – Semi-Finals and Final (Format Change)**  
*Applies to the final two rounds: semi-finals and final*

- **Team Participation**:  
  - The **semi-finals** involve **two teams** (the top two from the previous round).  
  - The **final** features the two semi-final winners.  
  - The **final is a double-leg format** (home and away), unlike earlier rounds.

- **Match Format**:  
  - **Semi-finals**: Played as **double-leg** (two matches: one at each team’s home).  
    - Aggregate score determines the winner.  
    - If tied on aggregate, extra time and then a penalty shootout apply.  
  - **Final**: Also a **double-leg** format.  
    - Same rules: aggregate score, extra time, penalty shootout if needed.  
  - **No away goal rule** applies in either.

> ✅ **Visual cue**: Red = format shift to double-leg; high-stakes final; aggregate scoring; visual emphasis on structure change.

| Phase | Color | Teams | Match Format | Key Notes |

| Second Set | 🟦 Blue | 60 teams (4 join) | Single-leg | 4 additional teams join |
| Rounds 3–5 | 🟩 Green | Halved each round | Single-leg | Knockout; no new teams |

text: The De Gennes Prize, previously called the Prize for Materials Chemistry, was established in 2008 and is awarded biennially by the Royal Society of Chemistry for outstanding and exceptional contributions in the field of materials chemistry. The prize honors the legacy of Pierre-Gilles de Gennes. The recipient receives £5000, a medal, a certificate, and completes a UK lecture tour. Pierre-Gilles de Gennes was born in Paris, France, in 1932 and graduated from Ecole Normale in 1955. He then worked as a research engineer at the Atomic Energy Centre (Saclay) before spending a brief period at the University of California, Berkeley and 27 months in the French Navy. He later became an assistant professor at the University of Paris in Orsay, where he conducted research on superconductors and liquid crystals. In 1991, de Gennes was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his studies on the boundary lines between order and disorder in materials such as liquid crystals. text: The Design Museum of Chicago, formerly known as the Chicago Design Museum, is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization founded by Tanner Woodford in 2012 as a pop-up museum, hosting exhibitions in various Chicago venues during 2012 and 2013. Following a successful Kickstarter campaign in 2014, it opened a permanent location in the Block 37 building. In late 2018, the museum relocated to Expo 72 at 72 E. Randolph St. Its mission is to "educate, inspire, and foster innovation through design." The museum operates through collaborative, community-based programs, largely dependent on local volunteers for exhibit design, curation, registration, marketing, and other core functions, with its foundation rooted in the visions and labor of these volunteers. It promotes free, open, and honest engagement with diverse audiences through a permanent collection, rotating exhibitions, and educational programming. Exhibitions cover a broad, cross-disciplinary definition of design, including graphic design, architecture, urban planning, interior design, and systems thinking. In 2021, the museum partnered with the Chicago Department of Public Health and the Chicago Department of Cultural Affairs and Special Events to commission over 80 local artists to create original art exploring themes of health, vitality, community, and vaccine distribution, which is displayed on print and digital billboards across Chicago neighborhoods and on social media. text: "Deșteaptă-te, române!" is the national anthem of Romania, originating from a poem written during the Wallachian Revolution of 1848. The lyrics were composed by Andrei Mureșanu and first published in 1848 under the title "Un răsunet," as a lyrical response to Vasile Alecsandri's poem "Către Români," later known as "Deșteptarea României," which influenced Mureșanu's work. The original text was written in the Romanian Cyrillic alphabet and was first sung in late June 1848 in the Șcheii Brașovului neighborhood of Brașov, where it quickly became the revolutionary anthem. The melody was originally a sentimental song called "Din sânul maicii mele" composed by Anton Pann, and Mureșanu selected it after Gheorghe Ucenescu, a church singer from Șcheii Brașovului, suggested it. The anthem has been sung during major Romanian conflicts, including the 1989 anti-communist revolution, and was officially adopted as the national anthem on 24 January 1990, replacing "Trei culori." This date marks the end of the communist era and follows the Romanian Revolution of December 1989. The song was also used during the brief existence of the Moldavian Democratic Republic (1917–1918) and served as Moldova's national anthem from 1991 to 1994 before being replaced by "Limba noastră." The anthem has eleven stanzas, but only the first, second, fourth, and last are sung on official occasions, with the full version performed on National Holiday (1 December) and accompanied by a 21-gun salute when the President is present. The overall message is a "call to action," likened by Nicolae Bălcescu to the French revolutionary song "La Marseillaise," due to its urgent demand for change. The anthem was banned after the Communist Party abolished the monarchy in December 1947, though it was later permitted under Nicolae Ceaușescu's regime without official recognition. It was first performed during the Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878) and World War I, and received heavy radio broadcast following the Romanian coup d'état of 23 August 1944. The song is also associated with the Union of the Principalities (1859), where "Hora Unirii" by Vasile Alecsandri was widely sung to the tune of a round dance by Alexandru Flechtenmacher. 29 July is observed annually in Romania as National Anthem Day (Ziua Imnului național).

text: Awaken, Romanian, rise from your deathly sleep, a trance induced by tyrannic barbarians; you await a new destiny, now or never is the moment to exact caustic shame and chagrin upon your enemies. Now or never, prove to the world your traditions, for in your veins still flows the blood of the Roman; within your minds and essence lies a name you proudly uphold—Triumphant in war, you are named after Trajan. Lift your broad forehead and observe the surrounding ranks, standing like ancient mountain fir trees, a hundred thousand brave warriors, ready to attack like wolves from the high mountains and wide plains, both old heroes and young soldiers. Behold the magnificent shadows: Michael, Stephen, Corvinus—the Romanian nation, your children, fearless. Armed with weapons, hearts fervent and aflame, we cry out: "Live in liberty or die." You were defeated at Milcov, in the Carpathians, by blind disunity; yet we, whose souls were pierced by sacramental liberty, swear to forever remain united in fraternity. A widowed mother from the time of Michael the Almighty demands today a helping hand from her sons, her eyes filled with tears and spewing blasphemy, as anyone who falters in this great peril will be cursed by her. Thunder, lightning, and brimstone shall consume those who escape this glorious calling; those who flee will be condemned, for when homeland and mothers, sorrowful in heart, call us to traverse through swords and fire, we will answer. Have we not endured enough of the cruel crescent's yataghan, whose fatal wounds we still feel today? Now the knout invades our ancestral lands, but the Lord is our witness—thus, we will cast it aside. Have we not suffered enough under despotism's blinding gaze, a yoke we have carried for ages like cattle? Now the cruel ones, in arrogance, seek to take away our language, but only the dead would surrender it. Romanians of the four rims, now or never, unite in reflection and emotion; proclaim to the world that the Danube has been stolen through intrigue and coercion. O Priests, rise with your holy cross, for this army is Christian; our motto is liberty blessed with sacred mission. Better to die in battle with pride and glory than to once again be slaves on our ancient land. Отбрось оковы, сердце румынского народа, восстань от векового, от мертвенного сна! Уже настало время зажечь огонь свободы и за свои страданья врагам воздать сполна! Уже настало время низвергнуть гнет тирана, принесший столько горя и зла краям родным. Пусть целый мир узнает: мы — правнуки Траяна, и чести славных предков вовек не посрамим! Как сосны вековые, стоят стеной солдаты, готовы с грозным кличем помчаться на врага, разя за край родимый, за гордые Карпаты: без родины свободной нам жизнь не дорога. О Михай, Штефан, Матьяш, великие владыки, не стыдно нам, потомкам, в глаза вам посмотреть: в руках мечи сверкают, огнём пылают лики, как гром, призыв суровый: «Свобода или смерть!» Погибель принесли вам кровавые раздоры, сердца сковала ваша жестокая вражда, но мы клянемся смело: ни реки и ни горы не смогут разделить нас, мы — братья навсегда! Мать Михая-героя, вдова, стоит пред нами, на славный подвиг ратный благословляет нас, но будет ею проклят с презреньем и слезами, кто дрогнет и отступит в тяжелый этот час. Мы за тебя готовы пройти сквозь сталь и пламя, Румыния, веди нас, сражаться нам вели! Пусть тех, кто сердцем будет с коварными врагами, Господь огнём и серой сотрет с лица земли! Довольно мы страдали от черных ятаганов, нам не страшны удары позорного кнута. Вставайте же, румыны! Долой ярмо тиранов! Свобода, честь отчизны навек для нас свята. Пусть враг нас хочет сделать скотиной бессловесной, похитить речь родную и мудрость наших книг, на смертный бой пойдем мы, ряды смыкая тесно, и не пленит захватчик свободный наш язык! Сыны земли румынской, забудем разногласья, единой силой встанем за милый отчий край, и о злодействе новом заявим громогласно: в руках убийц коварных великий наш Дунай! Благословенна будет грядущая расплата, священный, вечный подвиг — спасти страну свою. Мы вызволим отчизну из рабства супостатов или падем со славой в отчаянном бою!

text: Diane Crump (May 18, 1948 – January 1, 2026) was an American jockey and horse trainer. On February 7, 1969, she became the first woman to compete as a professional jockey in a pari-mutuel race in the United States, riding a horse named Bridle 'n Bit at Hialeah Park Race Track. Her participation faced intense hostility, requiring a full police escort through an angry crowd of shouting people, with hecklers yelling things like "Go back to the kitchen and cook dinner." Crump finished 9th in the 12-horse race and later recalled that her excitement allowed her to overcome the negative attitudes of male jockeys, trainers, and owners. Two weeks later, she won her first race. She was inspired to apply for a jockey's license in the fall of 1968 after Kathryn Kusner, the first woman licensed as a jockey, won a lawsuit against the Maryland Racing Commission for gender-based denial of a license; although Kusner was injured shortly after receiving her license, Crump stepped forward. Throughout 1968, female jockeys faced significant resistance; for example, W. L. Lyons Brown, a part owner of Churchill Downs, requested Crump not compete there due to anticipated controversy, and Penny Ann Early was denied the chance to ride because male jockeys boycotted her races. Two other women had been forced out of races after male jockeys threw rocks at their trailers and threatened a boycott. The situation at Hialeah changed when track officials threatened sanctions against male jockeys. In 1970, Crump became the first woman to ride in the Kentucky Derby, winning the first race on the undercard and finishing 15th in a 17-horse field on a horse named Fathom. By the time she retired from racing in 1985, she had ridden to 235 wins, though Equibase officially credits her with 228. She received invitations to ride in Puerto Rico and Venezuela; in a 1970s Puerto Rican race, she hit a male jockey with her whip after he held onto her saddle, and he eventually pulled away to win. On February 1, 1989, Crump suffered a serious riding accident in which she was crushed under her horse, breaking her leg in six or seven places, her ankle, and ribs, requiring ten days in the hospital and leading doctors to say she would never ride again. After recovery, she returned to riding, but accumulated injuries over the years ultimately led to her permanent retirement in 1999. She briefly retired in 1985 to focus on family, working as a farm trainer at Calumet Farm in Lexington, Kentucky, for over three years, and later trained horses at the Middleburg Training Center in Virginia starting in 1991. She resumed riding in 1992 and competed through 1998 before retiring in 1999. She ran an equine sales business and lived in Virginia. Crump was married to trainer Don Divine from 1969 to 1987. In 2020, a biography titled Diane Crump: A Horse Racing Pioneer's Life in the Saddle by Mark Shrager was published. In 2025, she was diagnosed with glioblastoma, and her family launched a GoFundMe to cover medical expenses. She died on January 1, 2026, in Winchester, Virginia, at the age of 77.

### 🔹 **1. Richard Whiteley’s Death (26 June 2005)**

**Before 2005:**  
Richard Whiteley hosted *Countdown* for 23 years, building its iconic status and loyal audience. The show was stable, well-known, and consistently popular, with strong viewer engagement and a trusted on-screen presence. The team included Carol Vorderman, Cathy Hytner, and a rotating group of lexicographers.

**After 2005:**  
Whiteley died after a failed heart operation. The show was postponed as a mark of respect, and no episode aired that day. Viewership dropped sharply, and the show entered a period of instability. A tribute was aired, and the programme went into a short hiatus (from 1 July) to decide on the next steps. This marked the beginning of a shift in hosting and audience trust.

---

### 🔹 **2. Carol Vorderman’s Departure (December 2008)**

**Before 2008:**  
Carol Vorderman had been the show’s long-standing assistant presenter and "vital statistician" for over two decades. She handled letter and number tile selection, verified calculations, and was a familiar, trusted face. Her role was central to the show’s structure and appeal.

**After 2008:**  
Vorderman left the show after being offered a 90% pay cut — a move reportedly seen as a sign of declining value. Her departure created a major shift in the show’s dynamic. Rachel Riley took over her role in January 2009, marking the end of an era and the beginning of a new generation of presenters and assistants. The show’s tone and style changed slightly, with less of Vorderman’s signature presence.

---

### 🔹 **3. Susie Dent Becomes Permanent Lexicographer (2005)**

**Before 2005:**  
Susie Dent joined in 1992 as a rotating lexicographer. The role was frequently filled by different experts, with no single person holding it long-term. Dictionary Corner featured rotating celebrity guests and lexicographers, often from Oxford or production staff.

**After 2005:**  
Susie Dent became the show’s sole, permanent lexicographer. From 2005 onward, she appeared regularly in "Dictionary Corner" and was credited as a co-presenter from January 2015. This gave the show a more consistent intellectual tone and helped solidify its educational reputation. Her presence became a key part of the show’s identity.

---

### 🔹 **4. Des Lynam Takes Over (October 2005)**

**Before 2005:**  
The show was led by Richard Whiteley, with strong viewer loyalty and high ratings. The format and tone were stable and familiar.

**After 2005:**  
Des Lynam became the new main presenter after Whiteley’s death. The show initially drew strong viewership — around 1.7 million daily — a drop from Whiteley’s era. However, his tenure was short-lived (until December 2006), and his demanding schedule led to public backlash when Channel 4 proposed moving filming closer to his home. Viewers objected, and he resigned, leading to a period of uncertainty.

---

### 🔹 **5. Des O'Connor Takes Over (January 2007)**

**Before 2007:**  
The show had just lost Whiteley and Lynam. There was a gap in leadership, and the team was adjusting. Susie Dent was on maternity leave during winter 2007–2008, and Alison Heard temporarily filled in.

**After 2007:**  
Des O'Connor took over as host. His tenure was marked by a brief but noticeable drop in viewership. By July 2008, both he and Carol Vorderman announced they would leave at the end of the year. text: Richard Huemer (January 2, 1898 – November 30, 1979) was an American animator active during the Golden Age of Animation. While working as an artist-illustrator in the Bronx, New York City, he began his animation career at the Raoul Barré cartoon studio in 1916. In 1923, he joined the Fleischer Studio, where he developed the Koko the Clown character, redesigned the clown for more efficient animation, and reduced the studio’s reliance on the Rotoscope for smooth motion. He created Ko-Ko's canine companion, Fitz, and established the drawing style that defined the series. After moving to Hollywood, Huemer worked as an animator and director at the Charles Mintz studio, where he developed the character Scrappy. He later joined the Disney Studio, remaining there from April 16, 1933, to February 28, 1973, with a three-year break from 1948 to 1951 during which he pioneered animated TV commercials and co-created with Paul Murry the comic strip The Adventures of Buck O'Rue. Huemer collaborated extensively with Joe Grant on several projects, including Fantasia (as story director), Dumbo (as screenplay), and various propaganda films supporting the U.S. war effort in World War II. Notably, Huemer and Grant submitted Dumbo to Walt Disney not as a completed storyboard, but as a series of storyboard "chapters" ending in cliffhangers, a strategy that successfully generated Disney’s interest in the project. In February 1973, Huemer was presented with a Mousecar by the Disney Studio during a ceremony attended by fellow animators. He received the Winsor McCay Award at the Annie Awards in October 1978, introduced by Ward Kimball. On October 10, 2007, Huemer's son, Dr. Richard P. Huemer, accepted the Disney Legends award in his father's name.

text: This discography outlines the musical works of the German rock band Die Toten Hosen, including their pseudonyms Die Roten Rosen and Tangobrüder. The band has sold more than 18 million records, with certified sales exceeding 14.5 million units in Germany, establishing them as one of the country’s best-selling music acts. Their most successful release is the compilation album Reich & sexy, which has sold over 1.1 million copies. Both Reich & sexy and their ninth studio album Opium fürs Volk became million-sellers in Germany and are among the best-selling albums of the 1990s in the country. The video album Nur zu Besuch: Unplugged im Wiener Burgtheater, with over 100,000 copies sold, is one of the best-selling video albums in Germany. By September 2023, the band had released 15 studio albums and eight live albums, along with nine compilation albums, three of which were produced for international markets. Among these, Love, Peace & Money and Crash-Landing are collections of the band’s songs featuring newly written English lyrics. Beyond these, they have released more than 70 singles and two EPs. The members have also contributed to albums by other artists, appeared on numerous compilations, and participated in radio, television, and film productions as guest musicians or extras. Eight songbooks containing sheet music and lyrics have been published. By December 2017, the band had released a total of 365 original compositions and over 168 cover versions. To mark their 30th anniversary, the studio album Ballast der Republik was released in May 2012 and immediately reached number one in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. In May 2017, the band achieved their tenth number-one album in Germany with Laune der Natur; by now, that number has risen to twelve, making them one of the most successful musicians in the German-speaking world. The band’s first charting album was released in 1987 under the pseudonym Die Roten Rosen, titled Never Mind The Hosen – Here’s Die Roten Rosen. In 1990, Auf dem Kreuzzug ins Glück became their first studio album to reach number one in the German charts. With Auswärtsspiel in 2002, the band topped the Austrian charts for the first time. Their most commercially successful single until 2012 was Zehn kleine Jägermeister (1996), which reached number one in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland and was certified platinum in Germany for over 500,000 sales. In 2012, the single Tage wie diese reached number one on the German Singles Chart and sold more than 990,000 copies across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since their formation in 1982, Die Toten Hosen have maintained almost the same lineup: Campino on vocals, Andreas von Holst and Michael Breitkopf on guitars, and Andreas Meurer on bass. Starting with the album In aller Stille in 2008, Vincent Sorg has been responsible for producing their music. Die Toten Hosen produced their first two singles and debut album Opel-Gang on their own label, Totenkopf, which was managed by Jochen Hülder and Trini Trimpop. Hülder remained the band’s manager until his death in 2015. In 1983, the band signed with EMI, which financed the video for Eisgekühlter Bommerlunder and a concert tour. text: Different World is the debut studio album by Norwegian DJ and record producer Alan Walker, released on 14 December 2018 through MER Musikk and Sony Music Entertainment, and includes his successful 2015 single "Faded". The album follows a trilogy of singles titled World of Walker, consisting of "All Falls Down", "Darkside", and "Diamond Heart". It was nominated for Top Dance/Electronic Albums at the 2020 Billboard Music Awards. Featuring artists such as Steve Aoki, Noah Cyrus, and Digital Farm Animals, the album combines recognizable tracks like "Faded" with new material such as "Lost Control". Walker stated that releasing the album was an "incredible feeling" and described it as a significant milestone after years of work, expressing excitement to share it with fans. A campaign titled "#CreateADifferentWorld" was launched to raise awareness about climate change. The first single, "Faded", features uncredited Naustdal pop singer Iselin Solheim and was released on 3 December 2015; it reached number one in Austria, Germany, Switzerland, and Sweden, was nominated for British Single of the Year at the 2017 Brit Awards, and won Årets Låt (Song of the Year) at the Spellemannprisen. The second single, "Sing Me to Sleep", also featuring Iselin Solheim, was released on June 3, 2016, and reached number one in Norway and number one on the iTunes charts in seven countries. "Alone", featuring uncredited singer Noonie Bao, was released as the third single on December 2, 2016, and charted internationally, reaching number one on the Norwegian Singles Chart. "All Falls Down", featuring Noah Cyrus and Digital Farm Animals, was released as the fourth single on 27 October 2017 and peaked at number one on the Norwegian Singles Chart and the US Billboard Dance Club Songs chart. "Darkside", featuring Antiguan-German singer-songwriter Au/Ra and Norwegian singer Tomine Harket, was released as the fifth single on 27 July 2018, with a remix by Dutch DJ Afrojack that reached number one in Norway and number 10 in Sweden. "Diamond Heart", featuring Swedish singer-songwriter Sophia Somajo, was released as the sixth single on September 28, 2018, with official remixes by Syn Cole and Dzeko; its music video was nominated for Best Cinematography at the 2019 Berlin Music Video Awards. "Different World", featuring American singer Sofia Carson, Norwegian music producer K-391, and Chinese music producer Corsak, was released as the album's lead single on November 30, 2018, coinciding with the "#CreateADifferentWorld" campaign and includes Walker's commentary on climate change; it reached number 31 in the Norwegian charts. Dancing Astronaut described the album as extending the fullest portrait of Walker's distinctive sound and a tightly threaded collection of songs that showcases his sonic artistry. Billboard called it a project that turns bleating synth melodies into sing-alongs, melts warm Caribbean rhythms with hardstyle booms, and electrifies the dance floor while aiming for radio readiness. Manuel Probst of Dance-Charts [de] noted that Walker's typical sound design runs through the album like a common thread, creating a melancholy atmosphere with attention to detail allowing each song to have a unique touch. Marit Johansen Jegthaug of NRK P3 criticized the album for having too few new songs, poor structure, lack of variety, and a lack of distinction between old and new tracks. Tor Martin Bøe of Verdens Gang gave it a "die throw" rating of 3 out of 6, describing it as "manic and gloomy" and stating the dark sense of abandonment feels "almost tacked on". Anjali Raguraman of The Straits Times described it as a "cinematic, vocals-driven album" and noted that it feels like Walker has played it safe by sticking to his familiar style. At the time of Billboard's 2019 mid-year report, the album had 93,000 equivalent album sales in the United States and "Faded" had 192,396,000 streams. text: Dina Nath Walli (1908–2006), also known by his pen name Almast Kashmiri, was an Indian watercolour artist and poet from Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley. He was a key figure in the modern art movement in Jammu and Kashmir and is recognized for painting everyday scenes of Kashmir. Born in 1906 in the Badyar Bala neighborhood of Srinagar, within the then princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, part of British India, he belonged to a Kashmiri Pandit family; his father passed away when he was very young. He received his early education in Srinagar and later completed a three-year course at Amar Singh Technical Institute, Srinagar, before moving to Calcutta in the Bengal Presidency in 1930 for further artistic training, where he studied various art forms under Percy Brown, the principal of the Government College of Art & Craft at the University of Calcutta. In 1936, he returned to Srinagar and focused on landscape painting in watercolours. He was awarded gold medals by the government of Kashmir in 1939 and received a highly commended medal from the Academy of Fine Arts, Calcutta in 1940. He also produced an album containing 12 paintings. Under the pen name Almast Kashmiri, his emphasis on realistic art and people's poetry is evident in his two poetry collections: Bala Yapair (This side of Mountains, 1955) and Sahaavukh Posh (Desert Flowers, 1981).

text: Gannon Stauch (September 29, 2008 – January 27, 2020) was an American boy who was murdered by his stepmother, Letecia Hardin (then Stauch), in Colorado Springs, Colorado. His disappearance and death drew national attention and prompted a large-scale search effort involving multiple law enforcement agencies and volunteers. Gannon was reported missing by his stepmother on January 27, 2020, when she told the El Paso County Sheriff's Office that he had left home between 3:15 p.m. and 4 p.m. to walk to a friend's house but never returned. The initial press release described him as a "juvenile runaway," but three days later, the sheriff’s office reclassified the case as a missing or endangered person due to new information. The search involved thousands of hours of investigation and hundreds of public tips, with assistance from the FBI Child Abduction Rapid Deployment team, the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, and the Colorado Springs Police Department. Search teams used drones, dogs, horses, helicopters, and divers to search various areas. Gannon's biological parents made emotional pleas for his safe return and thanked the community for their support. On March 2, 2020, Letecia Stauch was arrested in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, on charges of first-degree murder of a child by a person in a position of trust, child abuse resulting in death, tampering with a deceased human body, and tampering with physical evidence. She was extradited to Colorado and held without bond at the El Paso County jail. According to the arrest affidavit released on May 5, 2020, Letecia Stauch killed Gannon in his bedroom on the day he went missing, stabbing him 18 times, hitting him in the head with an object, and shooting him with a handgun. She then cleaned up the crime scene and disposed of his body in a suitcase, lying to investigators about her whereabouts and activities. She claimed Gannon was sick and stayed home from school, and drove with him to various places, but surveillance footage showed she left home with Gannon in her truck around 10:15 a.m. and returned with him around 2:19 p.m. On March 17, 2020, Gannon's remains were found by a maintenance worker under Escambia Bay Bridge in Pace, Florida, more than 1,300 miles from his home. The cause of death was blunt force trauma, sharp force injuries, and a gunshot wound. Investigators believe Letecia Stauch transported his body to Florida by driving there in a rented van after initially dumping it in a remote location north of Colorado Springs and retrieving it later. Letecia Stauch pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity and claimed she had dissociative identity disorder due to childhood sexual abuse. She also accused her husband of being involved in Gannon's death, alleging he had connections to drug cartels and sex trafficking rings, but was found competent to stand trial by a state mental hospital and her claims were dismissed by the court as unfounded. Her five-week trial concluded on May 8, 2023, with the prosecution presenting testimonies from Gannon's father, Letecia's former employers, family, investigators, forensic experts, and state psychiatrists. The defense offered Dorothy Otnow Lewis, a controversial psychiatrist specializing in dissociative identity disorder, as their sole witness. The jury rejected both the insanity defense and Otnow Lewis' testimony, and Letecia Stauch was found guilty of all charges. text: Disney Channel is an American pay television channel and the flagship property of Disney Branded Television, a unit of the Disney Entertainment business segment of the Walt Disney Company. Launched on April 18, 1983, as The Disney Channel as a premium channel on top of basic cable, it initially targeted families due to the availability of home television sets at the time. It dropped "The" from its name in 1997, rebranding as Disney Channel, shifting its focus to children and adolescents aged 6–14. The channel broadcasts original first-run children's television series, theatrically released and original television films, and selected third-party programming. As of November 2023, it is available to approximately 70 million pay television households in the United States, down from its peak of 100 million in 2011. Its international footprint, which once included 46 channels in 33 languages, has declined in parts of Europe and most of the Asia-Pacific due to the launch of Disney+ and competition from streaming and social media platforms. The channel launched nationally at 7:00 a.m. Eastern Time on April 18, 1983, under The Disney Channel, with founding president Alan Wagner helping to develop it; it became available in all 50 U.S. states by September 1983 and reached over 611,000 subscribers by December 1983. It debuted its first made-for-cable movie, Tiger Town, in October 1983, earning a CableACE Award, and achieved profitability by January 1985, with 1.75 million subscribers by that time. In September 1990, TCI's Montgomery, Alabama, system became the first to carry it as a basic cable service. Between 1991 and 1996, more cable providers transitioned it from a premium add-on to a basic tier, though Walt Disney Company executives denied plans to convert it into an ad-supported basic service, calling the shift part of a five-year "hybrid" strategy. On April 6, 1997, it officially rebranded as Disney Channel, though it was occasionally marketed as "Disney" from 1997 to 2002. Television films were produced under Disney Channel Premiere Films starting with Tiger Town in 1983, until October 1997, when the label was replaced with "Disney Channel Original Movies" (DCOM), with the first DCOM being Under Wraps, which premiered on October 25, 1997. The most successful DCOM in terms of popularity and accolades is High School Musical 2, which debuted on August 17, 2007, to 17.2 million viewers, setting a longstanding record for the highest-rated television premiere on the channel. Following it, the second-highest-rated DCOM premieres were Wizards of Waverly Place: The Movie, Camp Rock, Descendants 2, Princess Protection Program, Teen Beach Movie, and Jump In!. It previously held the record for the most-watched basic cable program until December 3, 2007, when ESPN surpassed it with an NFL game. The Cheetah Girls franchise was notably successful in merchandise and sales, with its 2003 debut film premiering to over 84 million global viewers and its sequel to 8.1 million American viewers, becoming the most successful film in the series; an 86-date concert tour featuring the group was ranked among the top 10 concert tours of 2006, selling out with 73,500 tickets in three minutes at one point. Disney Channel holds rights to theatrically released feature films, some shared with sister network Freeform, including films from Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures (such as Walt Disney Pictures, Walt Disney Animation Studios, and Pixar), and also features films from Bagdasarian Productions like The Chipmunk Adventure and Alvin and the Chipmunks Meet Frankenstein, though most are not currently owned by Disney. Between programming and ads, the channel features bumpers, with the creator of the four-note mnemonic introduced in 2002 being Alex Lasarenko, identified by the YouTube documentary channel Defunctland in 2022. ESPN's broadcasts of the Little League World Series have included cross-promotions with music-related Disney Channel properties such as High School Musical, the Jonas Brothers, Camp Rock, and Phineas and Ferb. In March 2023, Disney Channel broadcast a live professional sporting event for the first time, airing a youth-oriented alternate broadcast of an NHL game—the Big City Greens Classic—as part of ESPN's coverage, themed around the animated series Big City Greens and visualizing player and puck data with 3D animated players. Disney Jr. is a daily morning program block for preschoolers, succeeding Playhouse Disney, which launched on April 6, 1997, as part of Disney Channel's morning lineup. On May 26, 2010, Disney General Entertainment Content (then Disney-ABC Television Group) announced the expansion of the block into a 24/7 cable and satellite channel that debuted on March 23, 2012. The channel is commercial-free and competes with other preschool-focused channels like Nick Jr. and Universal Kids (formerly PBS Kids Sprout and Sprout). It features programming from Disney Channel's preschool library and films from the Walt Disney Pictures film library. On its launch, Disney Junior took over the channel space previously held by Soapnet, a Disney-owned network for soap operas, due to the decline of that genre and the rise of on-demand and digital viewing. Soapnet ceased operations on December 31, 2013. The Playhouse Disney block on Disney Channel rebranded as Disney Junior on February 14, 2011, and international channels followed; the names were shortened to "Disney Jr." on June 1, 2024, though pronounced the same. Disney-ABC Television Group had planned to launch a Playhouse Disney-branded channel in the U.S. in 2001 but never did, despite launching it internationally. Disney XD, launched on February 13, 2009, as the successor to Toon Disney, targets young audiences aged 6 to 14, including girls, and features action and comedy programming from Disney Channel and the former Jetix block, along with original and syndicated shows. Unlike Disney Channel and Disney Junior, Disney XD operates as an ad-supported service, similar to Toon Disney. The "XD" in its name has no official meaning, despite being associated with a former Disney.com mini-site called Disney Xtreme Digital. Disney Channel Animation, also known as "Disney Channel Animation," is the television animation production studio division of Walt Disney Studios based in Glendale, California, producing original animated programming for the three main Disney-branded television channels. A live-action production studio based in Studio City, Los Angeles, provides original sitcoms and comedy programs primarily for Disney Channel, with many projects co-produced and financed by the Walt Disney Company. Walt Disney EMEA Productions Limited, located in London, England, co-produces original programs in Europe with other companies. Disney Original Documentary is a banner from Disney Branded Television for documentary programs broadcast on Disney Channel and released on Disney+, launched on December 9, 2021. In 2010, Disney Channel All Star Party was released for the Nintendo Wii, a four-player mascot party game with stages resembling board games featuring characters from shows like Sonny with a Chance, Wizards of Waverly Place, and JONAS L.A. Several video games based on the Phineas and Ferb series were released by Disney Interactive Studios, and the Disney Channel website included Flash games with characters from franchises such as Kim Possible and Hannah Montana. In June 2012, the Walt Disney Company announced it would stop advertising or promoting food or beverage products that do not meet strict nutritional guidelines, making Disney Channel the first media company to take such a stance on junk food marketing to children; advertising appears only as underwriter sponsorships during promotional breaks. On July 1, 2012, Disney Channel began providing Descriptive Video Service audio in compliance with the 21st Century Communications and Video Accessibility Act of 2010, offering audio descriptions for the blind in the 25 largest markets and on the five highest-rated cable and satellite channels, including Disney Channel. This is indicated by an on-screen mark and a 2-tone sound repeated three times at the start of episodes of Gravity Falls, Austin & Ally, Good Luck Charlie, and Phineas and Ferb, and on newer episodes of Little Einsteins on Disney Junior (with ABC placing the mark in the bottom-left corner). Disney Channel has a presence in various regions across the Americas, most of Europe, the Middle East, Africa, India, and Japan, with former channel versions available or used in Australia, New Zealand, Italy, the United Kingdom and Ireland, Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, Turkey, Spain, and Brazil, though most ceased broadcasting in the early 2020s, with content moving to Disney+ or Disney+ Hotstar. On December 14, 2022, Disney ceased distributing programs in Russia in response to the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine. The channel licenses its programming to certain broadcast and cable channels outside the U.S. (including formerly Family Channel in Canada), regardless of whether a localized feed exists. Some critics have disapproved of Disney Channel's marketing strategy led by Anne Sweeney, president from 1996 to 2014, who focused programming on preteen and teenage girls and reduced animated content. In 2002, nearly all Walt-era and pre-1990s programming was removed from the channel, including the late-night "Vault Disney" block, which previously dominated the schedule since 1983. In 2008, Sweeney stated that Disney Channel, through its multi-platform marketing using television and music, would become "the major profit driver" for the Walt Disney Company. text: Doab (English: /ˈdoʊɑːb/) is a term used in South Asia for the tract of land lying between two confluent rivers and is similar to an interfluve. According to the Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary, R. S. McGregor notes its Persian origin, defining it as do-āb (دوآب, literally "two [bodies of] water") as a region lying between and reaching to the confluence of two rivers. In North India and Pakistan, where numerous Himalayan rivers divide the plains into doabs, the Indo-Gangetic plains consist of alternating regions of river, khadir, and bangar. Areas near rivers are low-lying floodplains, typically fertile khadir, while higher-lying areas away from rivers are bangar, less prone to flooding but generally less fertile. Khadir is also known as nali or naili, especially in northern Haryana, where it refers to the fertile prairie tract between the Ghaggar river and the southern limits of the Saraswati channel depression, which floods during rains. Within the bangar area, barani refers to low-rain areas where rain-fed dry farming is practiced, now often dependent on tubewells for irrigation; the Bagar tract, a dry sandy region on the border of Rajasthan adjoining Haryana and Punjab, is an example of barani land. Nahri refers to canal-irrigated land, such as the Rangoi tract, which is irrigated by the Rangoi channel/canal built to carry floodwaters from the Ghaggar river to dry areas. Historically, villages in the doabs have been officially classified as khadir, khadir-bangar (mixed), or bangar for centuries, with agricultural tax rates based on a tiered land-productivity scale. The Doab specifically designates the flat alluvial tract between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers, extending from the Sivalik Hills to their confluence at Prayagraj, also known as the Ganges-Yamuna Doab or Ganga Doab. This region covers about 23,360 square miles (60,500 square km), measuring approximately 500 miles (805 km) in length and 60 miles (97 km) in width. During the British Raj, the Doab was divided into three administrative districts: Upper Doab (Meerut), Middle Doab (Agra), and Lower Doab (Allahabad). Currently, the Doab includes the following states and districts: Dehradun and Haridwar; Saharanpur, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Baghpat, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Gautam Buddh Nagar, and Bulandshahr; Etah, Kasganj, Aligarh, Agra, Hathras, Firozabad, Mainpuri, and Mathura in the trans-Yamuna Braj region; and Farrukhabad, Kannauj, Etawah, Auraiya, Kanpur (Urban & Rural), Fatehpur, Kaushambi, and Allahabad. In the Punjab region of Pakistan and India, each doab has a distinct name, said to have been coined by Raja Todar Mal, a minister of Mughal emperor Akbar. These names (except "Indus Sagar") are formed by combining the first letters in the Persian alphabet of the rivers that bound the doab, from east to west. For example, "Chaj" (چج) = Chanāb (چناب) + Jehlam (جہلم). The Sind Sagar Doab lies between the Indus and Jhelum rivers; the Chaj Doab lies between the Jhelum and Chenab rivers; the Rachna Doab (a considerable portion of which is Majha) lies between the Chenab and Ravi rivers; the Bari Doab (a considerable portion of which is Majha) lies between the Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej rivers; the Bist Doab (or Doaba) lies between the Beas and Sutlej rivers; and the Raichur Doab, a triangular region in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka between the Krishna River and its tributary the Tungabhadra River, is named after the town of Raichur.

text: "Doki Doki Morning" is a song by the Japanese heavy metal band Babymetal, released in Japan as an independent DVD single on October 22, 2011, and serves as the first single from their debut album Babymetal. The song introduced all three members to heavy metal music; Nakamoto noted she had never heard such musical heaviness before, while Mizuno initially preferred dancing over singing. During production, the signature Kitsune hand gesture (similar to the sign of the horns) was developed. Vocals for the song were recorded on October 30, 2010. It first appeared in the Sakura Gakuin album Sakura Gakuin 2010 Nendo: Message, released on April 27, 2011, as part of the Jūonbu ("heavy music club") sub-unit. A limited-edition DVD single was announced on October 12, 2011, and later released as a standard digital download on October 22 and 23, 2011, available for pre-sale at the Sakura Gakuin Festival 2011 held at Mt. Rainier Hall "Shibuya Pleasure Pleasure," and subsequently sold in limited quantities on ASmart, Amazon, Tower Records Online, and Tower Records Shinjuku starting October 24. The limited edition included a DVD with the "Doki Doki ☆ Morning" music video and a cut focusing on the choreography for live performances, along with a towel embossed with either the band's logo or the Juonbu Records label. A CD single was released on April 6, 2012, packaged with a T-shirt. The song was later released as a promotional single in the United Kingdom on December 13, 2015. The track features a "modern heaviness" sound with dark, atmospheric instrumentals that transition into a catchier, brighter melody, including lyrics such as "Rin rin rin! Ohayō, wake up" (Ring ring ring! Good morning, wake up). Kikuchi highlighted that the tone contrasted directly with Japanese kei-on music (light music), leading the band to form under the Jūonbu label to signify this difference. Nakamoto, whose vocals were recorded separately from Mizuno and Kikuchi, needed to speak quickly and clearly in the verses. The song peaked at number 80 on the Billboard Japan Top Independent Albums and Singles chart for the week dated November 7, 2011. Directed by Shimon Tanaka, the music video shooting was completed by October 2011; Nakamoto mentioned that Tanaka wanted to appear in it but found the choreography difficult. The abridged version of the video was released on the Toy's Factory YouTube channel on October 12, 2011, with the full version posted on the official Babymetal channel on November 8, 2012. Metal Injection ranked the music video at number nine on "The Top 15 Metal Viral Videos of the Year" on December 8, 2011. The song premiered at the Sakura Gakuin Festival 2010 concert at Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse No. 1 on November 28, 2010. Su-metal recalled that during the interlude of the first performance, the group pretended to fall to the ground, fearing embarrassment, but the audience's positive reaction made her feel happy and affirmed her identity as Su-metal and Babymetal. On March 4, 2012, fellow Sakura Gakuin members Marina Horiuchi, Ayaka Miyoshi, and Airi Matsui covered the song as a "Shuffle Unit" during the Sakura Gakuin concert Sakura Gakuin Hōkago Anthology at the Nihonbashi Mitsui Hall. On December 8, 2013, Hana Taguchi, Saki Ooga, and Aiko Yamaide covered it as another "Shuffle Unit" at the Sakura Gakuin 3rd Anniversary: Live at the Amuse Musical Theater. Kiba of Akiba covered the song on the joint single "Babymetal × Kiba of Akiba." Credits are adapted from the album liner notes of Sakura Gakuin 2010 Nendo: Message and Babymetal.

### 🔗 **Cause-and-Effect Chain: From Fund to Medal**

**Cause:** The *International Darwin Memorial Fund* was established to honor Charles Darwin and promote biological research.  
→  
**Effect:** In 1885, the fund was transferred to the *Royal Society*, which became the institutional steward of Darwin’s legacy.  
→  
**Effect:** The Royal Society used the fund’s resources to *establish the Darwin Medal* as a formal recognition of excellence in evolutionary biology.  
→  
**Effect:** The medal was first awarded in 1890 to Alfred Russel Wallace, recognizing his independent development of natural selection — a direct contribution to Darwin’s work.  
→  
**Effect:** Since then, the Darwin Medal has served as a lasting symbol of the Royal Society’s commitment to advancing research in evolution, biological diversity, and developmental biology.  
→  
**Effect:** The medal’s design, eligibility, and awarding frequency reflect both Darwin’s scientific legacy and the evolving needs of biological research — ensuring continuity and relevance over time.

---

### 📚 Why This Strategy Works for Learning

- **Clear Historical Flow**: The chain shows how a financial and commemorative fund (originating in honor of Darwin) evolved into a tangible scientific award (the medal), making the connection between past and present concrete.
- **Causal Clarity**: Each step logically follows the previous one — no gaps or assumptions — helping learners understand *why* the medal exists and *how* it connects to Darwin’s life and work.
- **Retention Boost**: Linking the fund’s purpose (promote biological research) directly to the medal’s function (recognize excellence in biology) strengthens memory through meaningful context.
- **Contextual Depth**: It ties together key facts (dates, recipients, design, eligibility) within a coherent narrative, making the information more memorable and meaningful.

---

### ✅ Summary in One Sentence

> The International Darwin Memorial Fund, established to promote biological research, was transferred to the Royal Society in 1885 and directly led to the creation of the Darwin Medal — a biennial (later annual) award recognizing outstanding contributions to evolutionary and biological sciences, thus creating a lasting cause-and-effect link between Darwin’s legacy and modern scientific recognition.

---

text: Dolly, a female Finn-Dorset sheep born on 5 July 1996 and died on 14 February 2003, was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell. She was created at the Roslin Institute in Scotland by Keith Campbell, Ian Wilmut, and colleagues from the University of Edinburgh and PPL Therapeutics, using a technique called somatic cell nuclear transfer, where a nucleus from a mammary gland cell was transferred into an unfertilized egg cell that had its nucleus removed. The resulting hybrid cell was stimulated to divide and, when it developed into a blastocyst, was implanted into a surrogate mother. Dolly was the first clone produced from a cell taken from an adult mammal, proving that genes in a mature, differentiated somatic cell can revert to an embryonic totipotent state and develop into a whole organism. Although not the first animal ever cloned—John Gurdon had previously used adult somatic cells to clone African clawed frogs in 1958—Dolly gained widespread media attention as the first such clone from an adult mammal. She lived at the Roslin Institute throughout her life, where she was bred with a Welsh Mountain ram and produced six lambs: Bonnie in April 1998, twins Sally and Rosie in 1999, and triplets Lucy, Darcy, and Cotton in 2000. In 2001, at age four, she developed arthritis, which was treated with anti-inflammatory drugs, and by 2003, she had a progressive lung disease, specifically ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (Jaagsiekte), caused by the retrovirus JSRV. No link between her cloning and the disease was found, as similar cases occurred in other sheep in the flock. Dolly was euthanized at six years old, which is shorter than the typical 11–12-year lifespan of a Finn Dorset, though her telomeres were found to be short, leading some to speculate she had a genetic age of six. However, Roslin scientists found no evidence of advanced aging or health defects from cloning. After her death, her body was preserved via taxidermy and displayed at the National Museum of Scotland. In 2016, a study of 13 cloned sheep, including four from the same cell line as Dolly, found no long-term health issues beyond minor osteoarthritis, concluding there was no detrimental effect of cloning on aged offspring. Following Dolly’s success, many large mammals were cloned, including pigs, deer, horses, and bulls, though some attempts, like cloning argali, failed. Cloning efficiency was initially very low—Dolly was the only adult lamb from 277 attempts—and Wilmut later stated nuclear transfer may never be efficient for human use. By 2014, Chinese scientists achieved 70–80% success rates in cloning pigs, and by 2016, Sooam Biotech was producing 500 cloned embryos daily, while commercial pet cloning services like Viagen charged $50,000 for a dog, $30,000 for a cat, and $85,000 for a horse. Cloning has potential applications in preserving endangered species and reviving extinct ones; in 2009, scientists cloned the Pyrenean ibex, the first extinct animal to be cloned, though the newborn died shortly after birth due to lung defects. In 2016, four clones of Dolly—Daisy, Debbie, Dianna, and Denise—were alive and healthy at nine years old, and were later euthanized in 2017 after research showed they were aging normally. Scientific American noted that Dolly’s main legacy was in advancing stem cell research, including the discovery of induced pluripotent stem cells. In 2000, researchers cloned a lamb named Diana with a human gene for alpha 1-antitrypsin, which was activated in her mammary gland to produce therapeutic milk. In 2018, Chinese scientists created the first cloned primates, Zhong Zhong and Hua Hua, using the same method as Dolly. In 2019, five gene-edited cloned monkeys were created using CRISPR-Cas9, intended for medical research. In 2003, Belgian artist Dominique Goblet published a comic strip titled “2004 Apparition de Dolly dans la campagne anglaise” about her.

Many attractions focus on the history and culture of the Southern Appalachian region. The park features a variety of attractions, including Showstreet Palace Theater and Celebrity Theater, Dolly's Tennessee Mountain Home, Back Porch Theater, Smoky Mountain River Rampage, Dollywood Grist Mill, Valley Theater, Eagle Mountain Sanctuary, Wings of America Theater, Robert F. Thomas Chapel, Calico Falls Schoolhouse, Tennessee Tornado, Blazing Fury, Daredevil Falls, craft exhibits, the 3 ft (914 mm) narrow gauge Dollywood Express steam train, Imagination Playhouse, Village Carousel, The Amazing Flying Elephants, Lemon Twist, Shooting Star, Sky Rider, The Waltzing Swinger, Piggy Parade, Busy Bees, Lucky Ducky, Dolly's Demolition Derby, The Scrambler, Mystery Mine, Thunderhead, Drop Line, Whistle Punk Chaser, Lumberjack Lifts, Rockin' Roadway, Pines Theater, Lightning Rod, Barnstormer, Behind the Seams and Song-teller Museums, The Plaza at Wilderness Pass, Wild Eagle—America's first winged coaster—and FireChaser Express, a dual-launch coaster. Two new seasonal events debuted, and Dollywood's Splash Country added the TailSpin Racer mat racer slide complex. Sideshow Spin and River Battle were removed. In October 2019, Dollywood announced its first new festival in 14 years, Dollywood's Flower & Food Festival, featuring 10 to 15 foot tall topiaries based on Dolly's songs like "Coat of Many Colors," photo opportunities, a rainbow sky over Showstreet, and food. The festival was originally scheduled for May 8 to June 14, 2020, but was deferred to May 7 to June 13, 2021. In October 2019, Dollywood filed plans for a new resort adjacent to Splash Country and DreamMore Resort, featuring a 310-room hotel, a 325-seat restaurant, and a conference space, creating 100 jobs. In June 2021, Dollywood announced a $500 million expansion, including details about the HeartSong Lodge & Resort, which will have 302 rooms, five floors of suites, a four-story atrium with a large central fireplace, and multiple shopping and culinary experiences. HeartSong Lodge is scheduled to open in 2023, along with campgrounds, three additional resorts, and a "record-breaking" attraction. Two extra parking toll booths (four attendants) and additional staging lanes were added to reduce wait times. ## 🔍 Learning Strategy: "Feature vs. Full OS" Contrast

This strategy helps distinguish between:
- **A full operating system (OS)** — one that includes all essential components (kernel, user interface, system services, application frameworks, etc.) and can run a complete set of applications.
- **A feature-rich component or base system** — a minimal or core system that provides foundational capabilities (like kernel, networking, process management), but lacks higher-level features (GUI, app frameworks, desktop environment).

By applying this contrast, we can clearly identify:
- What Darwin **is** (a core Unix-like base),
- What Darwin **is not** (a full macOS),
- What features it supports,
- What features it lacks,
- And how it differs from the full macOS experience.

---

## ✅ Applying the "Feature vs. Full OS" Contrast to the Document

### 🟩 What Darwin *Is* (Feature-Level Core System)

Darwin is **not** a full operating system in the traditional sense. It is a **minimal, open-source core system** built on Unix-like foundations. It provides the essential **technical infrastructure** of macOS and other Apple operating systems.

#### ✅ Features of Darwin (Core, Foundational, "Feature-Level")
| Feature | Explanation |
|--------|-------------|
| **XNU Kernel** | A hybrid kernel combining Mach (microkernel), FreeBSD (networking, process model), and IOKit (device drivers). This gives performance and flexibility. |
| **POSIX Compatibility** | Supports POSIX APIs via its BSD lineage (mainly FreeBSD), allowing many Unix/Linux programs to run without modification. |
| **Networking Support** | Includes mDNSResponder (core of Bonjour), enabling zero-configuration networking. |
| **Service Management** | Uses `launchd` — an advanced service manager for starting/stopping system services. |
| **Hardware Support** | Supports modern architectures: x86-64, ARM (iPhone 5S+, iPad Pro, Apple Silicon), PowerPC (legacy). |
| **Open-Source Availability** | Source code is publicly available under the Apple Public Source License (APSL), enabling community forks and modifications. |

> 💡 These are **core system features** — foundational to any OS, but not sufficient to run a full desktop or app ecosystem.

---

### 🔴 What Darwin *Is Not* (Missing Full OS Capabilities)

Darwin **lacks** the higher-level components required to function as a **complete, user-facing operating system**.

#### ❌ Missing Features of a Full OS
| Missing Feature | Why It Matters |
|----------------|----------------|
| **No GUI (Graphical User Interface)** | Darwin does not include Aqua, Quartz Compositor, or any desktop environment. You cannot use Finder, Dock, or System Preferences. |
| **No Application Frameworks** | Missing Cocoa and Carbon APIs — the core frameworks used to build macOS applications. Without these, Mac apps cannot run. |
| **No Desktop Environment** | No window manager, desktop shell, or user interface elements. |
| **No Pre-installed Applications** | No Safari, Mail, Photos, etc. — no user-facing software. |
| **No macOS-Specific Services** | While it has `launchd`, it lacks the full suite of macOS services (e.g., Spotlight, Time Machine, iMessage, iCloud). |
| **Cannot Run Mac Applications** | Apps built for macOS (e.g., Final Cut Pro, Xcode) require Cocoa/Carbon and the GUI stack — which Darwin lacks. |

> ⚠️ This means: **You cannot use a Darwin system as a daily operating system** — it's not usable for end-users.

---

### 🔄 How Darwin Relates to Full macOS

| Aspect | Darwin | macOS |
|-------|--------|--------|
| **Core Kernel** | XNU (shared) | XNU (same) |
| **User Interface** | ❌ No GUI | ✅ Aqua + Quartz |
| **App Frameworks** | ❌ No Cocoa/Carbon | ✅ Full frameworks |
| **Application Support** | ❌ Cannot run Mac apps | ✅ Full app ecosystem |
| **User Experience** | Command-line only | Full desktop experience |
| **Certification** | Never certified as POSIX-compliant | Certified as SUSv3 (since Leopard) |
| **Availability** | Only as source code (no bootable installer since 2005) | Full, ready-to-use OS with installer |

> 📌 **Key Insight**:  
> Darwin is the **"engine"** of macOS — the underlying Unix-like foundation.  
> macOS is the **"vehicle"** — the complete, polished, user-friendly OS built on top of Darwin.
